b: Edit: I get Godzilla and the themes in the movie are about nuclear fallout, I don't think anyone actually read the post, because the scientist and the oxygen destroyer arey main focus here and nobody mentioned either
To start, this is just about the 1954 film, no other Godzilla movie or iteration is included in this viewpoint
I have heard time and time again about how Godzilla is a representation of the fallout of the nuclear bombs and what that means for the world now that nuclear bombs mean.

Then I watched the OG 1954 movie, and that's not what I got from it at all. Godzilla attacks japan, they struggle to kill him, then a scientist makes a machine that is able to kill Godzilla and they kill him. However the themes around Godzilla and this scientist are the opposite of what I have been told. This scientist makes a device called "the oxygen destroyer" it is not explained how the device does this, but it is just said that the device destroys all surrounding oxygen atoms. The scientist holds this device and it's existence with a ton of weight and secrecy. The scientist knows that this device could destroy the world if used too much or in the wrong hands. When they go to kill Godzilla, the scientist stays, purposely killing himself, and the knowledge of how to make the oxygen destroyer going with him.

So we have a story where out of nowhere something comes and attacks the country, the country does everything they can to stop it, then a scientist comes up with a potentially world ending device to end that threat.
To me, that sounds like World War 2, but with Godzilla being japan, the scientist being Oppenheimer, and the oxygen destroyer being the nuclear bomb.

Unlike the oxygen destroyer in the movie, the nuclear bomb wasn't kept secret, and the scientist didn't take the knowledge with him. The movie to me seems to be about how America should have handled the nuclear bomb, showing that they were too reckless and let this insanely powerful device continue to be made and have the knowledge of how to make them, be let out. Instead saying that they should have completely ended all knowledge of how to make the nuclear bomb once they were used.
